title: The Remote — Sc147: family pile on the sidewalk, neighbour rants back (in-file cut)

source.github: mhvnsnt/cn-gigaleak-gumball, draft release untagged-1676e192ae8c72e95791, asset id 640772406
source.method: FLA (XFL zip) read via sequential local-header parser (2012 Flash zips have malformed central directory); DOMDocument.xml + LIBRARY symbol XMLs parsed directly. Same neutral per-keyframe transform format as production/dance-choreo v1: a part pose is (item, first_frame, affine matrix a/b/c/d/tx/ty, pivot). keyMode 9728 = pose-to-pose; sampled_frames hold each keyframe's elements to the next keyframe, matching SWF playback.

teaches: Two held tableaux joined by a cut INSIDE the scene file: the background layer swaps at frame 42. First, the Wattersons sit in a heap on a photographic suburban sidewalk -- Richard reclined on the ground, Nicole, Gumball and Darwin clustered over him -- and hold it for ~41 frames with only face-comp micro-variation (the whole group is one nested symbol, 'animation', on a single 'family' layer; there are zero scene-level body-puppet keyframes in the file). Then the file cuts to the neighbour (a stock CROWD_GUY build) alone in his driveway, arms up and mouth wide in a shout that he holds, with slow settling, for the remaining ~105 frames. The lesson is reaction-shot economy: when the joke is 'they stare / he yells', build one group nest and one solo hold, and let a background keyframe do the cutting.
notes: One scene file, two setups: the background layer is keyframed at frames 0 and 42 -- a family group tableau on a suburban street, then an in-file cut to the neighbour alone in front of a different house.

The entire family performance is nested inside a single master symbol named 'animation' on the one 'family' layer; the builder's cast entry therefore groups the face comps of Gumball, Darwin, Nicole (MOM) and Richard under one entry -- there are no scene-level puppets at all (0 body-puppet kf vs 929 face-comp kf).
The neighbour is a stock crowd build (CROWD_GUY_01_FV_COMP on the 'neighbour' layer) given a 100+-frame solo hold: arms up, mouth wide, settling only in the last ~20 frames.

Render cost was the highest in this batch: ~25-30 s/frame even from the video-stripped copy -- the nested family symbol plus full-res photo plates; the frames were completed in two ranged FFDec exports (see NOTES gaps).
